paragraphs.source_en: There was a thing to the light, to the hills, the road," said the Martian. "I felt the strangeness, the road, the light, and for a moment I felt as if I were the last man alive on this world. . . ." "So did I!" said Tomás, and it was like talking to an old and dear friend, confiding, growing warm with the topic. The Martian closed his eyes and opened them again. "This can only mean one thing. It has to do with Time. Yes. You are a figment of the Past!" "No, you are from the Past," said the Earth Man, having had time to think of it now. "You are so _certain_. How can you prove who is from the Past, who from the Future? What year is it?" "Two thousand and one!" "What does that mean to _me?_" Tomás considered and shrugged. "Nothing." "It is as if I told you that it is the year 4462853 S.E.C. It is nothing and more than nothing! Where is the clock to show us how the stars stand?"
